dct_description_sm: Methlymercury (MeHg) in fish and seal is a concern for the Inuit people as these items are a large component of their country foods.  Exposure to MeHg is known to cause long-term developmental delays in children and has also been associated with cardiovasuclar health risks in adults.  Flooding associated with the creation of new reservoirs for hydroelectric development has been shown to increase bioaccumulation of mercury in fish and seals.  Development of a new reservoir has been proposed for the Lower Churchill river and is likely to affect mercury dynamics in the downstream (Lake Melville) environment.  To understand the impact of the development, we are developing an environmental fate and bioaccumulation model for Hg and MeHg in Lake Melville.
dct_subject_sm: Health sciences and contaminants -> Food consumption
dct_title_s: Mercury samples from Lake Melville, Labrador
